title: Building a Self-Updating Team Roster With GitHub Actions
excerpt: A small experiment in AI-assisted development: a single-page team roster kept up to date automatically by GitHub Actions and Discord.
html:
A couple of weeks ago, I explored AI-assisted development by building a small but meaningful project: a single-page team roster system.

The goal wasn't to build something complex, but to keep it lightweight, automated, and genuinely useful in day-to-day operations.

What it does:

  • A GitHub Actions workflow automatically updates the roster every week
  • Sends scheduled updates to a Discord channel
  • Supports manual overrides, like swapping team members when needed
  • Includes a simple configuration option to manage Discord integration dynamically

This project was more of an experiment to understand how far I can go with automation using GitHub Actions combined with a simple static setup.

What stood out to me is how even a static page can start behaving like a dynamic system when it's powered by the right workflows and automation. It also reinforced a simple idea: small systems, when designed well, can remove a surprising amount of manual effort.

Next, I'm planning to explore more complex applications using AI-assisted development, continuing to experiment and learn what's possible beyond simple automation.
